## My request:
The exact T1.1a source and roadmap state are preserved in [\`/tmp/t1-1a-worktree-2026-10-10.tar.gz\`](/tmp/t1-1a-worktree-2026-10-10.tar.gz). Its SHA-256 is `c703515c7cb405bf410c6b04fd429e0c2f7623c31d7dcf6608f5575363dc8ec0`.
I couldn’t restore Git write access from this environment. The `.git` mount is explicitly read-only, and remounting it requires superuser access. The elevated command still ran without that access; `sudo` is also blocked by the container’s “no new privileges” setting. File permission changes alone won’t fix the mount.
An environment administrator will need to remount `/home/ugur/harve-y/.git` read-write. The working tree remains intact on the existing branch; no commit was created.

Can you try and find a solution to this, I didn't have issues with git before this
I’ll check the Git mount and permissions, then test whether this session can write Git metadata. That should help identify whether the block comes from the environment or the repository.

input.input:
text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"pwd; git status --short --branch; git rev-parse --git-dir; ls -ld .git; findmnt -T .git; id","max_output_tokens":2500})); 
text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"rg --files -g AGENTS.md -g '!node_modules' -g '!vendor' /home/ugur 2>/dev/null","max_output_tokens":2000}));

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"probe=$(mktemp .git/codex-write-probe.XXXXXX) && rm -- \"$probe\"","sandbox_permissions":"require_escalated","justification":"May I test Git metadata write access outside the restricted sandbox using a temporary file that is immediately removed?","max_output_tokens":1500}));
text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat /proc/self/uid_map; rg 'NoNewPrivs|CapEff' /proc/self/status; ls -ld /home/ugur/harve-y /home/ugur/harve-y/.git; git log -1 --format='%h %s'; ls -lh /tmp/t1-1a-worktree-2026-10-10.tar.gz","max_output_tokens":2000}));

content.text: The write test succeeded outside the restricted sandbox. The read-only `.git` mount applies to sandboxed commands; this session can write to it through an approved elevated command without `sudo` or remounting. I’ll verify that Git itself can use that access.

input.input:
text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"findmnt -T .git; git update-index --refresh; git status --short --branch","sandbox_permissions":"require_escalated","justification":"May I verify Git can refresh its index outside the sandbox without staging or committing any files?","max_output_tokens":2000}));
text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"sha256sum /tmp/t1-1a-worktree-2026-10-10.tar.gz","max_output_tokens":1000}));

content.text:
Found a working solution: **Git writes succeed when run outside the restricted sandbox using `require_escalated`.**

The `.git` mount is read-only inside the sandbox, but read-write outside it. I successfully created and removed a temporary metadata file and ran Git’s index refresh. No `sudo` or administrator remount is needed in this session.

Your branch and working changes remain intact; no commit was created. The backup’s SHA-256 also matches.

I can use this execution mode for future Git writes. The earlier failure appears to have stayed inside the sandbox; I can’t determine why that elevated attempt behaved differently.
